main_text.p: mus ad Orientalium trutinam, momentif- que suis ponderemus, & videamus, quinam cohorrescere debeant, nos, an Veielius, Hot. tingerus, & qui ab ipsorum in hoc argumento stant partibus.

Hottingerus itaque in atenam animofe descendens, postquam pag. 28. num. 28. plura in genere sine vlla probatione, testimonio, vel auctoritate garriuit de Orientalium confensu cum Reformatis in capitibus fidei, ritibus, ac regimine Ecclesiastico, ad speciem tandem deueniens haec subdit: In specie vero vbi ad singulorum dogmatum dequentum fuerit examen, obseruamus, Orientales, vel Reformatis per omnia accedere, vel in circumstantijs tantum variare; vel vbi Pontificijs videntur fauere partibus; illud aut ex principijs fluere, Pontificiorum etiam opinione erroneis, aut φαγουδῶς potius quam ὄντως, verbis, quam rebus assensum testari maiorem. Atque sic non negamus, Orientales Ecclesias cum Romana aliquid habere simile (idem, difficulter obtinebunt). Hisitaq; vult Hottingerus, Orientales Ecclesias cum Romana aliquid habere simile, at non idem; φαγουδῶς, & non ὄντως; cum Reformatis vero ὄντως, & rebus. Hinc vero ad articulorum, in quibus consentiunt Orientales cum Reformatis, vt ait, concedens enumerationem ita scribit: Plu-

page.notes: The Greek word after "fauere" is printed as "φαγουδῶς" in the first occurrence and "φαγουδῶς" in the second; the exact letters are doubtful at this resolution and may read differently. Greek "ὄντως" is copied as best read. Marked the first Greek word for doubt in the transcription. Show-through and the left-edge dark marks are not printed text and are omitted. Printed "animofe" and "Hot." are kept as printed; "Hot." may be an abbreviation for Hottingerus, as printed. Long s is rendered as plain s throughout.
